title: Leeds ask fans to respect players breaking Ramadan fast at Elland Road
content:
Leeds United have asked fans to show respect towards players breaking their Ramadan fast during the team’s FA Cup fifth-round game against Norwich City on Sunday.

This comes after boos were heard around Elland Road on Saturday during Manchester City’s visit, while the away side’s Muslim players Rayan Cherki, Omar Marmoush and Rayan Ait-Nouri broke their fast during a stoppage in play.

Ramadan is a period observed by Muslims that involves not eating or drinking during the daylight hours before breaking their fast once the sun sets. Its dates are determined by the lunar cycle — this year, Ramadan began on February 17 and concludes on March 19.

During the game against City, a message was shown on Elland Road’s big screen that explained the break in play.

City manager Pep Guardiola called for “respect” after the game, while British anti-discrimination charity Kick It Out condemned the boos and described the reaction as “massively disappointing”.

In a statement published on Friday, Leeds confirmed that Saturday’s fixture against Norwich would again be paused after 5.56pm GMT on Sunday, around the 75th minute of the game, to allow players to break their fast, including their striker Joel Piroe.

“Leeds United Football Club explicitly condemn any supporters in the home or away sections who actively boo players observing Ramadan and use the protocol in place to break their fast,” the team said in the statement.

Leeds also took some responsibility for the incident during the City game, saying: “In hindsight, we should have been more proactive with our communications in advance of the Manchester City fixture to explain to supporters that this was going to happen, there was a clear lack of awareness by some attending the fixture.”

The club also said that the message displayed against City was not visible to 25 per cent of the stadium and that fans could have believed that City were taking advantage of a ‘tactical timeout’.
